title: an accent-composition branch read the following byte without checking one exists
object: the input buffer of length bytes, one direct allocation
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. SPATIAL row.
shape: a two-byte decode entered on the last byte of the input
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct g_malloc-family allocation, no wmem layer. GLib's g_malloc is malloc plus abort-on-failure.
fidelity: model consumer, real arithmetic: the sizes and the crossing expression are upstream's, quoted in PROVENANCE.md.
live_proof: absent at the pin: v4.6.8:epan/charsets.c carries `} else if (i < length - 1 && (*c & 0xf0) == 0xc0) {` (`grep -c` = 1). The form without the index check is at 3aad1ef236e6^ and is absent from the pin. A fix-reversal.

nested_why: the crossed buffer came straight from the platform allocator with no inner layer between -- wiretap, wsutil and ui do not use wmem, and epan/uat.c and epan/charsets.c take the crossed buffer from g_malloc or from the caller -- so under this inventory's axis, WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT, this row is NOT nested.
distinguishing: the guard that was missing is not a LENGTH check but an EXISTENCE check for the second byte of a two-byte sequence -- the loop's own bound is correct, and the branch simply consumes one more byte than the bound accounts for. That is why the fix adds `i < length - 1` to the branch condition rather than changing the loop.
